title: Beware the Fragile Ego: The Law of Envy
coreMove: Detect near-peer envy by tracking when praise, critique, distance, or concern begins to punish another person's rise.
sourcePressure: This law exposes envy as disguised corrosion: another person's success becomes a wound to the self, especially among peers and near-equals.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating envy as obvious jealousy instead of a disguised force that often speaks in support, taste, standards, or concern.

hook: a generic "people are not rational" opener for Beware the Fragile Ego: The Law of Envy
opening with a definition of the law
starting with a vague office conflict
counterintuition: the obvious lesson is wrong because people are complicated

exampleSpecs.domain: two pastry chefs shortlisted for the same magazine feature
exampleSpecs.audience: a chef noticing her critique has become personal
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether professional standards become a cover for sabotage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she underlines every comment about the rival's technique and crosses out the lines that are really about being passed over
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a proof sheet from a food magazine beside a sugared rolling pin

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate poetry workshop after one student's publication
exampleSpecs.audience: a peer group where admiration turns sour
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether critique becomes a socially acceptable attack
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the instructor pauses the critique and asks which objections were present before the acceptance email arrived
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stapled poem packet with one acceptance email printed on top

exampleSpecs.domain: a small architecture firm where a junior designer wins a public commission
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal tempted to call growth arrogance
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether mentorship turns into quiet obstruction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal reviews when his feedback shifted from precise design notes to character warnings after the commission
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foam building model casting a long shadow across a drafting table

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood running club after a new member qualifies for Boston
exampleSpecs.audience: a club captain managing rank pain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether jokes and concern isolate the faster runner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before naming envy, the captain calls it safety concern; after timing the comments, she sees they appear only after faster splits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a race bib pinned to a cork board under split times

exampleSpecs.domain: a newsroom book reviewer covering a former classmate's bestseller
exampleSpecs.audience: a critic whose taste language may hide comparison pain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether readers get criticism or resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reviewer hands the draft to an editor with one note: remove any line that only punishes the author's success
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a galley copy covered with yellow tabs

exampleSpecs.domain: a startup alumni network where one founder raises a large round
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder hearing concern used as a knife
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether useful caution becomes contagious bitterness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts the group will discuss fundamentals, then watches their concern focus only on the founder's visibility and praise
